production.note: US model years 2018-2023. Start: KBB's 2018 Model 3 specs list 'Model 3 Performance Sedan 4D'. Last: Car and Driver's specifications for the 2023 Model 3 Performance AWD (caranddriver-model-3-2023-specs, read by the project owner on 8 October 2026 (the site blocks the research tools)) and KBB's 2023 list ('Model 3 Performance Sedan 4D', kbb-model-3-2023); InsideEVs on the 2024 Performance: "which bests the outgoing model's 455 HP" (insideevs-model-3-performance-2024). The 2024-on car is tesla-model-3-performance-highland. yearSplit is set so the name carries the years and separates it from the Highland car; this car has no generation code in common use.

drivetrain.note: KBB 2018 and 2023: Drivetrain 'AWD' for the Performance; Edmunds 2023: 'Performance 4dr Sedan AWD (electric DD)'.

transmission.note: Edmunds 2023 Model 3: trim 'Performance 4dr Sedan AWD (electric DD)' (direct drive); drivetrain table 'Transmission: 1-speed direct drive' (shown for the Long Range).

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (magazine specification section; Tesla published no horsepower for these years). Car and Driver's specifications for the 2023 Model 3, read by the project owner on 8 October 2026 (the site blocks the research tools): "2023 Model 3 Performance AWD: 455 HP". InsideEVs agrees for the last pre-Highland car: "which bests the outgoing model's 455 HP" (insideevs-model-3-performance-2024). Car and Driver's road-test panel for a 2019 Model 3 Dual Motor Performance (pasted by the owner on 9 October 2026; link not supplied) gives "Combined Power (C/D est): 470 hp", a Car and Driver estimate.

weightLb.note: Car and Driver's specifications section for the 2023 Model 3 (the maker's figures, not a road-test measurement), read by the project owner on 8 October 2026 (the site blocks the research tools): "2023 Model 3 Performance AWD: ... 4048 lbs Curb weight". Weight-order step 2 (major magazine specification panel). Reference year 2023 is the earliest year with a step-2 weight; earlier figures are databases or tested: KBB 2018 4,072 lb (see discrepancies) and Car and Driver's 2019 road-test panel "Curb weight: 4072 lb" (tested, owner-read 9 October 2026, link not supplied).

discrepancies.reason: Model year. KBB's 2018 Model 3 Performance Sedan 4D: "Curb Weight | Not Available | Not Available | 4072 pounds"; Car and Driver's 2023 specification gives 4,048 lb. Car and Driver's tested 2019 car also weighed 4,072 lb.
discrepancies.resolution: Reference year 2023, the earliest year with a step-2 (magazine specification) weight, so 4,048 lb is used.

provisionalNote: Power (455 hp) rests on Car and Driver's specifications section for 2023 (read by the project owner, 8 October 2026) and InsideEVs; Tesla published no horsepower rating for 2018-2023, and other figures range 450-487 hp (Car and Driver's own test estimated 470 hp). A Tesla-published rating would replace it. Weight (4,048 lb, 2023) is a step-2 magazine specification figure. Body, drivetrain, transmission and the start year rest on KBB and Edmunds (databases).
